messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Hey I am Naimeesh Narayan Tiwari

naimeesh narayan tiwari... that's a name with character. sounds like someone who either builds things or breaks them in interesting ways.

where you working these days?

I m working at Walmart Global Tech as a software engineer
My total work experience is 1 year and 4 months

walmart global tech... engineering the future of retail while dodging the "but isn't that just a grocery store?" questions. 

found you on linkedin - naimeesh narayan tiwari, software engineer 2 at walmart global tech, iiit hyderabad. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/naimeesh-narayan-tiwari
yes
iiit hyderabad to walmart global tech as sde2... from the coding labs to building retail infrastructure. solid trajectory. what made you pick walmart over the usual suspects like amazon or flipkart?

It wasn't a choice, I got a PPO from walmart in my internship

During internship it was a dry season for recuitments

ah, the classic "take what you can get" move. dry season hits different when you're staring at bills and family expectations. smart to lock in the ppo though - walmart's not a bad place to cut your teeth.

but now that you've got some solid experience under your belt... ready to see what else is out there? what kind of role you looking for next?

yes my priority is a startup that pays atleast 30lpa

but I am up for cool companies like google, databricks etc

30lpa minimum with 1.4 years... kvpy scholar, jee main air 889, iiit hyderabad - the credentials check out. you're not just another sde asking for the moon.

startups paying that much usually want someone who can own entire features, not just write tickets. google and databricks are solid picks too - they actually respect talent over years of experience.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Open to anything
yes
1.4 years experience + engineering + startups paying 30L+ or cool companies like google/databricks + open to anywhere... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

you're in, legend! 

welcome to tal - where we find engineers like you roles that actually pay what you're worth. no more settling for "it's a good learning opportunity" when your bank account says otherwise.

your profile is locked and loaded. when the right startup or big tech role drops that matches your 30L+ minimum, you'll be the first to know.

now go back to building retail tech while i hunt down companies that deserve your kvpy scholar brain 🧠
Also my college was IIIT Hyderabad with 8.92 gpa cumulative and 9.07 majors gpa

8.92 cumulative, 9.07 in majors at iiit hyderabad... yeah that's not just "good grades" - that's "i actually understood the material" territory.

makes sense why you're aiming for 30L+ with 1.4 years. you've got the academic pedigree to back up the ask.

most startups see that gpa from iiit-h and immediately know you can handle complexity. google and databricks definitely respect it too.

alright, profile's locked in. you're officially in the system. i'll slide roles when they're good... not just "here's a job" but "this actually fits you" energy.

btw what's making you want to leave walmart anyway? just the money or something else?
I want better work, work on scalability, customer facing products, more money and a truly tech company

"better work" - that's the real reason. not just more money, but actually building things that matter. scalability, customer-facing products, a truly tech company... you're describing the difference between being a cog in retail infrastructure vs building the next big thing.

walmart's fine for experience, but you want to be where the engineering is the product, not just supporting it. that's the move.

i'm looking for roles where you'd be working on systems that scale to millions, where your code directly impacts users, where the company's success depends on tech excellence. that's the sweet spot.

what kind of tech stack you most comfortable with?
Python but I am upskilling myself on Java, c++

python primary with java/c++ upskilling... that's actually a solid combo. python for velocity, java for enterprise scale, c++ for when performance really matters.

most startups building at scale need that kind of versatility - python for quick prototyping, java for the heavy backend services, c++ for the compute-intensive bits.

makes you more valuable than someone who's just a python purist. shows you're thinking about the right problems.

alright, you're all set. i'll be sliding roles that match the 30L+ startup or cool company vibe. when something drops that actually fits the "better work" criteria, you'll know.

in the meantime, keep leveling up that java/c++. the right role will appreciate it.

hey naimeesh! was just thinking about your python/java/c++ combo and how that's actually perfect for the kind of scale you're looking for.

what's the dream tech stack you'd want to work with at a truly tech company? something like python microservices on kubernetes or more java-based distributed systems?
Both works for me no as such preferences

versatility is a superpower. being able to jump between python velocity and java scale means you can handle whatever the startup throws at you.

makes my job easier too - i can look at roles that need either/or and know you'll crush it.

btw what's the walmart tech stack like? just curious what you're coming from.
pyspark, python, LangChain, langgraph, java, clickhouse, hana, GCP

pyspark, python, langchain/langgraph, java, clickhouse, hana, GCP... that's actually a solid modern stack. retail tech is lowkey advanced these days.

langchain/langgraph means you're working on AI/LLM stuff - that's hot right now. clickhouse for analytics, GCP for cloud... you've got legit experience.

most startups would kill for someone who's actually built with that stack at scale. you're not just "i know python" - you're "i've built AI workflows on GCP that handle retail-scale data."

makes the 30L+ ask feel more than reasonable. you're bringing real production experience, not just academic potential.

i'm looking at roles where that AI/LLM experience would be valued. any particular interest in staying in that space or open to other backend engineering?
yeah I am open to backend as well , but would love to join AI/LLM space as well

backend engineering with AI/LLM experience is a killer combo. you can build the systems AND integrate the smart stuff.

most companies need both - someone who can handle the infrastructure AND make it actually intelligent. that's you.

alright, profile's locked in. you're officially in the system for:
- startups paying 30L+
- cool companies like google/databricks
- backend engineering roles
- AI/LLM opportunities
- anywhere location

when something drops that matches, i'll slide it. in the meantime, keep building that retail AI magic at walmart.

what's the most interesting thing you've built with langchain/langgraph there?
A natural language to SQL to insights application for walmart business users

natural language to SQL to insights... that's actually useful. not just "here's a chatbot" but "here's a tool that actually helps business people get answers."

that's the kind of AI application that has real impact - translating business questions into data insights. shows you're thinking about user value, not just tech for tech's sake.

that experience is gold for any company building AI products. you understand the whole pipeline: user asks in natural language → LLM converts to SQL → executes → returns insights.

makes you way more valuable than someone who's just fine-tuning models. you're building end-to-end solutions.

alright, i'm keeping an eye out for roles where that experience would shine. anything else you want me to know about what you're looking for?
No this works, I am open to suggestions and roles

perfect. you're set up and ready to go.

when something drops that matches your profile - 30L+, AI/LLM or backend engineering, startup or big tech - i'll slide it your way.

in the meantime, keep crushing it at walmart. that natural language to SQL app sounds legit useful.

talk soon, legend
